## HueMux v0.0.5-alpha.6 — The Mux tab

> **Alpha.** Built and tested in CI, and exercised on the nine Salon lamps on
> one real bridge. The Mux tab is the first version of the effect
> multiplexer; expect the primitive set and the layout to change.

### A lane mixer, not a node graph

The old Presets page answered whether a DAG could be represented. It did not
answer whether a phone could compose an effect in under a minute. The new
**Mux** tab is a lane mixer: each layer is one source, one effect, a blend, and
a level. The wiring is implicit, so there is nothing to position first.

- Add a layer from a short list of useful pairs: warm pulse, gradient, chase,
  sparkle, rainbow, sound pulse, video map, solid.
- Reorder with up/down buttons. No drag-only affordance.
- Edit while stopped: the preview clock keeps animating.
- **Start** applies the mix to the Salon lamps. **Stop** stops the clock and
  leaves the last frame up. **All off** explicitly blacks the room.
- Save and load presets from the same sheet.

The old node editor remains under the `full`/`sync` profiles. The Mux tab is
available under `lights` too, because it only needs light control.

### Sources and effects

Sources: **Timer**, **Sound**, **Video area**, **Constant**, **Random**.
Effects: **Solid**, **Pulse**, **Gradient**, **Chase**, **Rainbow**,
**Sparkle**, **Video map**.
Blends: replace, add, max, screen, multiply, over.

Every effect names the source value that drives it, so the same pulse can be
driven by a timer, a bass band, a beat, or the video average. The document is
plain JSON and survives a restart.

### Three decoupled Go layers

- `internal/mux` is pure: colors, sources, effects, lanes, blends, document
  validation. It has no HTTP, no Hue, no timers, and no wall clock. Given the
  same time and inputs, it produces the same output.
- `internal/muxrun` owns the clocks: a 12.5 Hz preview ticker that always
  runs, and a separate 1–10 Hz output clock (default 4 Hz) that only feeds the
  bridge while started. A slow bridge drops stale frames instead of queueing
  them.
- `internal/muxhue` adapts a frame to one combined `on` + `dimming` +
  `color.xy` PUT per changed lamp. It skips unchanged lamps and never talks to
  the bridge from the core.

The API is `GET/PUT /api/mux`, `GET /api/mux/state`,
`POST /api/mux/start|stop|off`, and `/api/mux/presets`.

### Only the Salon lamps

The multiplexer resolves the `Salon` room at start time and refuses to drive
anything outside it. This release sees nine colorable lamps there. Targets can
be narrowed per lane.

### A simpler icon

The six-strand gradient fan is gone. The mark is now three coloured inputs,
red, green and blue, merging into one output node. It stays legible at the
22px header size, which the old six-gradient mark did not. The generated SVG,
favicon, Android adaptive vector, AppImage PNG, and store icons all came from
the same geometry.

### If you reach HueMux by a DNS name

WebSocket upgrades are origin-checked. A host HueMux cannot derive, such as a
reverse-proxy vhost or a Tailscale MagicDNS name, has to be in
`allowed_hosts`:

```jsonc
{
  "allowed_hosts": ["huemux.lan", "luna-prime.tailnet.ts.net"]
}
```

The list is read per request, so a change takes effect without a restart. Raw
addresses this machine holds are accepted without configuration.

### Known limits

- The `video` source and `video_map` effect are implemented, but the
  `lights` profile has no screen-sync grid provider, so they stay inactive
  until a later phase.
- `sound` reads the server's existing 32-band analysis. The Mux page does not
  open a microphone yet; start a capture from the existing music surface until
  it gets its own button.
- REST output is the phase-one sink. Four updates per second suits pulses,
  gradients, chases and sparkles; it is not a strobe path. The entertainment
  stream is the next phase.
- The document format is version 1. It is meant to survive this alpha, but
  primitives and defaults can still change.

### Verification

`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), and
`gofmt` are clean. The Mux page was checked at 390×844 and 1280×720, including
starting and stopping the output and adding a layer. The live run addressed
only the Salon lamps, and every lamp was restored to its pre-test brightness
and colour afterwards.

### Updating

The Android app bundles the frontend, so take the APK from this release. A
desktop browser only needs a reload of the new service. `huemux.service` must
be restarted to serve the new embedded UI.
